In RFA Nos. 69 & 71 of 2021, applications have been filed for condonation of delay of 2373 & 658 days in re-filing &
filing the respective appeals, and in RFA No. 70 of 2021, applications have been moved for condonation of delay of 2373 & 441 days in re-filing & filing the appeal.
Notice of the applications was issued on 26.02.2021.

In two appeals bearing RFA Nos. 69 & 70 of 2021, separate replies to application for condonation of delay in filing the respective appeals on behalf of respondent-State stood filed and inter alia prayed for dismissal of the application being time barred.

I have heard learned counsel for the parties and gone through the contents of the applications,
which have been supported by the affidavits.

Concededly, the other similarly situated landowners pertaining to the same acquisition proceedings have already been held entitled for the modified amount of compensation pertaining to the acquired land falling in same revenue estate, i.e. Village Sarai Aurangabad, Tehsil Bahadurgarh, District Jhajjar, in view of judgment dated 17.11.2017 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal Dharambir And Ors vs State Of Haryana And Ors on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144728656/
2 No. 19354 of 2017, titled "Rajender Singh & Ors. Versus State of Haryana & Ors.".

MAIN APPEAL(S) This order shall dispose off present three appeals bearing RFA Nos. 69, 70 & 71 of 2021, as the same arise out of common acquisition.
[2] The appellants / landowners, by instituting the present appeals preferred under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short "the Act"), are seeking modification of the awards dated 14.06.2011 & 17.01.2012 passed by learned Additional District Judge, Jhajjar (hereinafter to be referred as "Reference Court") for enhancement of compensation amount.

[3] Briefly, the facts are that in pursuance to Haryana Govt. Notification under Section 4 of the Act issued on 17.04.2002, followed by Notification dated 10.04.2003 under Section 6 thereof, the land measuring 88.55 acres, including the land of appellants, situated in revenue estate of Village Sarai Aurangabad, Tehsil Bahadurgarh, District Jhajjar, was acquired.
The public purpose for acquisition of the land was stated to be development of residential and industrial sectors.

The Land Acquisition Collector, Jhajjar (for short "LAC"), vide Award No. 6, dated 25.06.2004, assessed the market value @ ` 3,50,000/- per acre for Chahi & Nehri land, whereas for the land of Brani and Gair Mumkin, the value was assessed @ ` 2,50,000/- per acre.

3 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:146026 RFA No. 69 of 2021 (O&M) Neutral Citation No.
2023:PHHC:146026 [4] Dissatisfied with the aforesaid Award, landowners / interested persons filed objections under Section 18 of the Act, which were decided vide awards dated 14.06.2011 &
17.01.2012 by Reference Court, whereby the market value for Chahi & Nehri land was enhanced /
assessed @ ` 4,50,000/- per acre, and for the land of Brani and Gair Mumkin and low lying land (Khada), the market value was assessed @ ` 3,50,000/- per acre alongwith other statutory benefits.

sentences.text: Aggrieved thereof, the appellants-landowners preferred their respective appeals.

[5] It may be mentioned here that the appeals preferred by some other landowners, were disposed off by this Court on 31.08.2015, lead case of which was RFA No. 1626 of 2011, titled "Puran Chand Wadhwa (deceased) through LRs Versus Land Acquisition Collector and another", whereby the value of the land of revenue estate of village Bahadurgarh was assessed @ ` 13,00,000/- per acre and for the land pertaining to other revenue estates, namely, Sarai Aurangabad, Balore and Bir Barktabad, the value was assessed @ ` 10,00,000/- per acre alongwith all statutory benefits.

[6] Against the judgment dated 31.08.2015 (supra), some landowners approached the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a batch of appeals, lead case of which was Civil Appeal No. 19354 of 2017, titled "Rajender Singh &
Ors. Versus State of Haryana & Ors.", which were allowed on 17.11.2017, whereby compensation for Village Sarai Aurangabad was enhanced from ` 10,00,000/- to ` 15,00,000/- per acre.

sentences.text: 3 [7] It is contended by learned counsel for the appellants that present appeals are squarely covered with the judgment dated 4 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:146026 RFA No. 69 of 2021 (O&M) Neutral Citation No. 2023:PHHC:146026 17.11.2017 passed in Rajender Singh's case (supra), arising out of the same notification vide which the land of appellants was acquired.

sentences.text:
[8]
Learned State Counsel is not in a position to dispute the afore-stated factual position about judgment dated 17.11.2017 passed in Rajender Singh's case (supra); however, opposes payment of interest for the period, the appellants failed to approach this Court.
[9] I have heard learned counsel for the parties and gone through the paper-book.

[10] From the records, it is apparent that the present appeals are squarely covered with the judgment dated 17.11.2017 of Rajender Singh's case (supra), which are arising out of the same acquisition / Notification dated 17.04.2002 covering the same revenue estate i.e. Village Sarai Aurangabad, Tehsil Bahadurgarh, District Jhajjar, whereby the landowners have been held entitled for the modified / enhanced amount of compensation @ ` 15,00,000/- per acre.

For reference, the relevant paras of judgment dated 17.11.2017 passed in case of Rajender Singh's (supra) reads as under:-
"

In the peculiar facts and circumstances of the cases, and considering the aforesaid evidence making deduction for development, it would be appropriate to award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- per acre for other villages i.e. Bir Barkatbad, Balore and Sarai Aurangabad alongwith statutory benefits.

Thus we enhance the compensation for Bahadurgarh from Rs.13,00,000/- per acre to Rs.20,00,000/- per acre and for other villages i.e. Bir Barkatbad, Balore and Sarai Aurangabad from Rs.10,00,000/- per acre to Rs.15,00,000/- per acre.
Appeals are allowed to the aforesaid extent.
Payment be made as expeditiously as possible preferably within six months. "

5 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:146026 RFA No. 69 of 2021 (O&M) Neutral Citation No.
2023:PHHC:146026 [10.1] Based upon the above, applying the principle of parity, besides award of just and fair compensation, the appellants-landowners being similarly situated are held entitled for grant of similar amount of compensation as has been awarded to other landowners vide judgment dated 17.11.2017 in case of Rajender Singh (supra), alongwith all other statutory benefits and interest thereupon as provided under the Act, except payment of interest for the period the appellants did not approach this Court after passing of Reference Court's Award.
